question: A can do a piece of work alone in 40 days. A and B together can do the same work in 10 days. C is 50% less efficient than B. In how many days can A and C together complete the same work ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM of 40 and 10 = 40 units.

Efficiency of A = 40 ÷ 40 = 1 unit/day and Efficiency of (A + B) = 40 ÷ 10 = 4 units/day.

Efficiency of B = 4 − 1 = 3 units/day.

C is 50% less efficient than B ⇒ Efficiency of C = 50% of 3 = 1.5 units/day.

Time for (A + C) = Total work ÷ Combined Efficiency = 40 ÷ (1 + 1.5) = 40 ÷ 2.5 = 16 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A alone = 40 days

Time taken by A and B together = 10 days

C is 50% less efficient than B.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

⇒ Efficiency of B = Efficiency of (A + B) − Efficiency of A

⇒ Efficiency of B = 4 − 1 = 3 units/day

⇒ Since C is 50% less efficient than B, C's efficiency = 3 − (50% of 3) = 1.5 units/day

⇒ Combined efficiency of A and C = Efficiency of A + Efficiency of C

⇒ Combined efficiency of (A + C) = 1 + 1.5 = 2.5 units/day

⇒ Time taken by (A + C) = Total Work ÷ Combined efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 40 ÷ 2.5 = 400 ÷ 25 = 16 days

**∴ The correct answer is 16 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work and Time Relationship

Time and efficiency are inversely proportional to each other. Total work completed is strictly equal to the product of efficiency and the time taken.

Joint Efficiency Principle

When multiple people work together without obstructing one another, their combined efficiency is simply the sum of their individual efficiencies (e.g., EffA₊B = EffA + EffB).

Percentage Efficiency Change

When a person is x% less efficient than another, their new efficiency is calculated as Base Efficiency × (100 − x) ÷ 100.
